heroHeadline: ASSK Moved to House Arrest Under Junta — NUG Demands Proof of Life; KIA Kills 40 in Shwegu; SAC Bombs Kill 5 Children Near India Border; KNLA Captures Thai-Border Base at Htee Khee
heroSubtitle: On Day 1,918 of Myanmar's civil war (May 4, 2026), four major developments emerged: (1) The junta's transfer of Aung San Suu Kyi from Naypyidaw Prison to house arrest (announced Apr 30-May 1) was rejected by the NUG and her son Kim Aris as a 'deceptive political maneuver,' with lawyers unable to independently verify her transfer; (2) KIA forces killed 40 SAC troops and captured 1 in Shwegu Township (Kachin State) after the junta deployed 1,000+ reinforcements including tanks; (3) A SAC jet from Tada-U Air Base killed 5 children aged 3-10 and 1 adult near the India-Myanmar border in Falam Township (Chin State) on May 1, triggering 150+ refugees to flee into Mizoram; (4) KNLA Brigade 4 captured the Htee Khee junta operation base on the Thai-Myanmar border in Tanintharyi Region after a week of fighting, with SAC troops fleeing into Thailand. Separately, the NUG Human Rights Ministry announced nearly 6,000 people — including 740 children — have been killed in SAC airstrikes since the 2021 coup; and 47 journalists remain in junta detention as of World Press Freedom Day (May 3). The SAC also launched a major ground invasion of Yinmabin, Pale, and Kani townships (Sagaing Region) on May 1. Myanmar's civil war — now in its fourth year — continues at maximum intensity across all regions.
footerNote: Data sourced from AAPP, ACLED, UN OCHA, Irrawaddy, RFA, Myanmar Now, DVB, Al Jazeera, Mizzima, Human Rights Watch, Crisis Group, Myanmar Peace Monitor, MoeMaKa CDM News, IMNA / Mon News Agency, CPJ, NPR, Northeast Live TV, Aryan Age, Myanmar Peace Monitor, NUG Ministry of Human Rights, Committee to Protect Journalists, and official NUG, KNU, KIA, AA, and PDF statements.
